newsitem.title: USA: Walbro Q1 hurt by start-up costs.
newsitem.headline: Walbro Q1 hurt by start-up costs.

text.p: Walbro Corp said Thursday its resutls for the first quarter were hurt by start-up costs for automotive production contracts that will begin later this year.

"Automotive operations also suffered from continued in-sourcing by a major customer in the first quarter," L.E. Althaver, chairman, said in a statement. "This in-sourcing should be completed by the end of the second quarter."
Earlier, Walbro reported first quarter earnings of $0.27 a share, down from $0.53 a year ago.
The company said second half 1997 earnings should begin to improve as new production contracts begin and its three-year period of heavy new plant and personnel investments starts to show results.

"We are confident that our shift in focus and combined structure, along with the start-up of several major production contracts, will result in improved earnings in the second half of 1997 and beyond," Althaver said.
Walbro makes precision fuel systems and products for automotive and small engine markets.
